metadata.note: ai-explainer PROGRESS RECORD for @HumanitariansAI, first-person Sanjana Rao (af_bella). Week of Oct 4-10, 2026: 85 videos / 13 fellows / Mycroft / 100% GitHub / 12 approved, 2 needs-mods. Framework = THE LAST MILE: clean finish / portrait holds / on GitHub -- the check between finished and shipped.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW -- ClaudeComposerAsk, ask answered; first-person Sanjana
beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Sanjana, a project manager at Humanitarians AI. This week I reviewed eighty-five fellow videos for the Mycroft project -- thirteen fellows, and every single one with its code already on GitHub. The old checklist was basically automatic. So only two came back. And here's the strange part: not for their content. For the last mile -- the part of a video that's easy to finish, and easy to miss.

props.command: I reviewed 85 fellow videos this week for the Mycroft project, and almost all of them passed. So what actually sends a finished video back?
output: code on GitHub + clean branding -- basically automatic now
what's left is the last mile: how the file actually plays
two went back -- a stray footer, and a broken 9:16

beats.role_note: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW -- hesitant-writer BLUF; corrects the reel's real misconception
beats.narration_text: Here's the whole idea in one breath. It's tempting to think a finished video is a shipped video. It isn't. The content can be done -- the explainer, the code, the branding all correct -- and the file still isn't ready. The last mile is how it actually plays, and that's exactly what I check before a professor ever sees it.

If the content is done, it ships.

beats.role_note: SHOW-DON'T-TELL: the week's throughput; the old gate is now automatic, so what's left?
beats.narration_text: Here's the week. Eighty-five videos, thirteen fellows, all on one project -- Mycroft. A year ago, what sent videos back was process: wrong resolution, wrong branding, no code committed. This week every one had its code on GitHub and clean branding. That gate is basically automatic now. So only two came back -- and both of them looked finished. The problem was never the content. It was the last mile.

shot.visual_intent: A film-strip of fellow-video frames with a throughput counter filling to 85; chips: 13 fellows | 1 project (Mycroft) | 100% on GitHub. Then the 'old gate' (resolution/branding/GitHub) lights all-green and reads AUTOMATIC; a terracotta question lands: 'so what sent 2 back?' -> THE LAST MILE.

beats.role_note: framework-first (PROOF): the 3 last-mile checks, shown BEFORE any example
beats.narration_text: So before a fellow video goes to the professors, I check the last mile -- three things. One: clean finish? No leftover toolkit footer or watermark baked into the render; the tool's chrome should never ship. Two: does the portrait hold? The nine-by-sixteen is its own layout, not a squeezed landscape -- no overlapping text. Three: is it on GitHub? Code and assets committed. Three pass, it goes up for the profs. Any fail, it goes back to the fellow with a mail.

shot.visual_intent: An export-style checklist (progress-bar rows, not badges): 1 CLEAN FINISH? (no baked-in footer vs a stray footer strip) 2 PORTRAIT HOLDS? (9:16 laid out on its own vs overlapping text) 3 ON GITHUB? (committed vs nothing pushed). Each row a green pass test + a red fail. Footer rule: 3 PASS -> UPLOAD FOR PROFS | any FAIL -> mail the fellow. Terracotta on the footer.

beats.role_note: ASK->RESULT LAW -- composer ask that runs this week's queue (-> T05 result)
beats.narration_text: Let's run this week's real queue. Fourteen reviews came in. Watch me take one through the last mile -- not the content this time, just how the file ships.

props.command: Here's this week's Mycroft queue -- 14 fellow reviews. Take each finished video through the last-mile check: clean finish, portrait holds, on GitHub. Flag anything that isn't upload-ready for the professors.

beats.role_note: worked example walked through the framework -- a clean submission clears all three
beats.narration_text: Take the first submission -- eight videos. Clean finish? Yes -- nothing baked into the frame that shouldn't be there. Portrait holds? Yes -- the nine-by-sixteen is laid out on its own, text clear. On GitHub? Yes. Three greens, so that one goes straight up for the professors to review. And most of the queue looked exactly like this -- twelve of the fourteen cleared on the first pass.

shot.visual_intent: A submission card 'Aishwariya Patil -- Mycroft -- 8 videos' with a small 16:9 screen pane. Three checks land green in order (CLEAN FINISH / PORTRAIT HOLDS / ON GITHUB), then a green verdict 'UPLOADED FOR PROFS TO REVIEW'. A quiet counter: 12 of 14 cleared first pass. Green accent on the verdict.

beats.role_note: falsifiability -- two finished-looking videos that fail DIFFERENT last-mile checks
beats.narration_text: Now the two that went back -- and here's the catch: both looked done. The first: eight videos, the content was solid, but a leftover toolkit footer was baked into the end of the render. Fails clean finish. The second: eight videos, the landscape cuts were genuinely nice -- but the nine-by-sixteen had text overlapping itself, hard to actually watch. Fails portrait holds. Neither failed on content. Both passed the old gate. The last mile is the only thing that caught them. So each gets a mail, a fix, and a second pass.

shot.visual_intent: Two submission cards side by side. LEFT 'Onkar Bhujbal -- 8' with a 16:9 pane showing a stray footer strip at the bottom, struck red -> red stamp FAILS CLEAN FINISH. RIGHT 'Ameya -- 8' with a clean 16:9 pane + a 9:16 pane whose caption text overlaps itself, struck red -> red stamp FAILS PORTRAIT HOLDS. Both note 'content OK | old gate OK'. Verdict strip: NEEDS MODIFICATIONS -- mailed. Terracotta/red on the two failures.

beats.role_note: reusable rubric restated -- CONTENT DONE -> last-mile gate -> UPLOADED
beats.narration_text: So here's the rule I carry into every review. Content done is not the same as shipped. The explainer can be finished, the code committed, the branding perfect -- and the file still fails at the last mile. The last mile is small, it's boring, and it's exactly where a good video gets caught before anyone important sees it.

shot.visual_intent: A clean router: LEFT 'CONTENT DONE -- explainer, code, branding'. A center gate = the three last-mile checks CLEAN FINISH / PORTRAIT HOLDS / ON GITHUB. RIGHT 'UPLOADED -- for the profs'. Footer punch: 'Done isn't shipped. The last mile is.' High negative space, terracotta accent on the gate.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW -- ClaudeComposerAsk 'Your turn.'; prompt read aloud + discussed
beats.narration_text: Your turn -- and this one's for the fellows. Before you submit your next video, run your own last mile. Paste this: ask Claude to build you a two-minute pre-submission checklist -- watch the final ten seconds for any stray footer or watermark, open the nine-by-sixteen on an actual phone and read every caption for overlap, and confirm the code and assets are pushed. A good answer gives you a short list you can tick before you hit send. Catch it yourself, and it never comes back with a mail.

props.command:
Act as my pre-submission reviewer for a fellow explainer video.
Build me a 2-minute LAST-MILE checklist to run on my OWN export:
1. CLEAN FINISH: scan the final 10s for any toolkit footer/watermark baked in.
2. PORTRAIT HOLDS: open the 9:16 on a phone; flag overlapping or clipped text.
3. ON GITHUB: confirm code + assets are committed and the link works.
Give me a tickable list + the 3 things that most often get a video sent back.
